status: proposal, awaiting Chanté's approval. Nothing here is canonical until approved; close-up assets are not generated. v1 (2026-09-13) was measured on the long-table painting (art/archived/scene_mockups/library-background-long-table.png); v2 (2026-09-13) redraws it on art/scenery/library/background.png, the painting the Library serves. The architecture is unchanged between the two (a pixel diff shows no change above the floor except the alcove's furniture and the window bay's seat), so slots, plaques, rows and close-up frames carry over; the reading circle, the floor anchors, the routes, the depth scale, the window bay and the chrome (the rail nav) are new.
about: The Library's camera-view manifest. Stable spatial IDs name physical places only; what a slot holds for a user (a Collection's name, a Thread Group's name) is data stored elsewhere, never here. The annotated maps in spatial-map/ are drawn from this file by scripts/draw-library-map.py, so edit the numbers here and redraw.

coordinates.convention: Normalized to the canonical wide painting: x 0.0 (left) to 1.0 (right), y 0.0 (top) to 1.0 (bottom). Rectangles are {x, y, w, h} with x, y at the top-left corner. Points are [x, y]; for Lumi a point is where her feet touch the floor or shelf. An anchor on a raised surface carries `floor_y` (the floor below it, which sets her depth scale) or an explicit `scale`.
coordinates.closeup_projection: Until a close-up is generated and measured, its geometry is the wide geometry projected into its frame: closeup = ((x - frame.x) / frame.w, (y - frame.y) / frame.h). A close-up must be generated as a detailed re-rendering of exactly its frame, so the projection holds. Once approved, measured close-up coordinates are added to that view under `measured` and take precedence.

source.note: The painting this geometry is measured on and the maps are drawn over.

depth_scale.note: v2 estimate, read by eye off the floor tiles' foreshortening (row spacing about 12px at y 0.72, about 32px at y 0.93, so the horizon is near y 0.40; an FFT of the floor was swamped by the sunlight stripes and settled nothing). It replaces v1's linear 0.42 at the back wall, read off the long table's furniture, which would make the alcove's armchair about four times the reading circle's. Cross-checks at this scale: the far doorway is about 3.6 of her, the ladder about 4.9, the alcove armchair about 1.35, the centre bay's drawer cabinet about 0.9. The reading circle's armchairs are about 0.6 of her: that furniture is painted at about half the scale of the alcove's armchair. Still an estimate: judge it on spatial-map/stills.png before any walking is drawn.

transitions.scale_to_frame: Acknowledge (the plaque warms, about 150ms). Then scale and translate the wide layer so target_region fills the stage (about 800ms, ease-in-out). Crossfade to the close-up asset over the last 250ms, aligned to the same rectangle. Thread Group plaques and Thread spines fade in after. Lumi may turn toward the slot or start walking; the camera never waits for her.
transitions.pull_out_to_parent: The reverse: the close-up scales down into its rectangle and crossfades to the wide layer. Back is a visible control as well as the browser's Back.
transitions.pan_to_thread_group: Inside a close-up: translate vertically so the chosen row sits in the readable band (about 500ms). Not a new view.
transitions.crossfade_via_table: Selecting a Thread ends spatial navigation: the view crossfades to library_table (about 400ms) and the book opens at once. Lumi's retrieval runs alongside and never delays it.
transitions.pull_out_to_origin: From the table, back to the Thread Group row it came from (or library_wide).
transitions.reduced_motion: Every transition becomes a 200ms crossfade; Lumi does not walk.
